name: Minimalism
visualIdentity: Explicitly described as Minimalism: retain only elements needed to communicate, with generous negative space, precise proportions, a limited palette, and consistent edges and spacing. The palette suggestion is optional, not a canonical definition.
suitableUses: Suitable for UI and product stories, editorial layouts, motion posters, and staged geometric compositions. It can support data or process explanations when each chart or diagram clarifies one idea. These are documented fits; choose based on the subject and goal.
limitations: Usually works best alone; hybrid styles can dilute it. Omit recomposition when it adds no explanation, crops important details, or forces text into unsafe areas. Avoid stacks that hide needed copy or provenance, and transitions that obscure causality or break a continuous-shot or loop requirement.
palette: When no task, brand, or approved reference palette exists, suggested tokens are background #FAF9F5, foreground #202421, and accent #406B5A. Keep them discrete; gradients are disabled. Preserve supplied colors, role assignments, asset colors, and style color limits. Recheck contrast on actual composites; listed ratios do not guarantee readability over images or effects.
motionAndInteraction: Use a few elements at a time, restrained easing, measured spacing, and reading holds; avoid relying on fades for every transition. Suggested restrained position changes and masks. For interactive HTML, optional scroll patterns include pinned internal recomposition, readable card stacking, chapter handoffs, or staged storytelling; use only when the action fits. Video must derive states from seekable composition time, not live scroll. Preserve backward/direct seek coherence and reduced-motion behavior.
audio: No fixed soundtrack or required audio layer. Choose music, voiceover, vocals, effects, ambience, or silence for the subject, audience, and explicit requirements. Keep speech intelligible, avoid competing vocals and clipping, and synchronize sound and picture; audio assets are unspecified.
assetRequirements: Use a small set of real text and graphic elements. Exact copy, fonts, imagery, and other supplied assets are unspecified. Load local fonts and assets, preserve approved colors and artwork, and state missing or unverified inputs. Inspect actual frames and decoded output for legibility, crop, timing, and synchronization.
combinations: Usually use Minimalism alone. For quantitative or structural explanations, style-097 can provide one honest chart per scene, with supplied data and no decorative values; style-109 can provide sparse process outlines with consistent stroke and accent only on the active path. Preserve the stated palette and avoid clutter.
productionApproach: Build visuals with HTML/CSS and SVG as needed; use one motion owner per animated property. HyperFrames is the primary composition, timing, sync, validation, and export pipeline. Remotion is allowed only if unavailable or a verified limitation blocks a required capability, with reason recorded. The pipeline does not own visual design. For video, inspect key frames and watch the full output.
